# A nice mental jaunt

### *[BrainFi Gets in Your Head](https://bradydale.com/series-brainfi-gets-in-your-head.html)*

Here's something I wish I understood: Before the pandemic, I was lightly interested in science-fiction. I grew up on superhero comic books, which are *like* science-fiction. So I was interested in science-fiction as a genre of literature related to the content of comic books.

But I wasn't particularly interested in sci-fi itself. I read a lot of Robert Heinlein in high school, for reasons maybe I will go into another time. I read a lot of fantasy in middle school. But other than Kurt Vonnegut, I didn't much care about sci-fi.

But something changed in the pandemic, and I can't quite retrace my steps now.

I got interested in aliens. I got interested in psychic phenomena. I wanted to read the people who had done the best job speculating about these things in a way that I hadn't cared to before. If I really reach, I can find inklings of this interest beginning. I listened to a lot of episodes of *Last Podcast on the Left* before 2020, for example. I could kind of describe to you theories about how what it meant for an extraterrestrial to appear "real" got a bit murky.

But something really kicked in after 2020. It became a fixation.

![](https://bradydale.com/blyg/media/2b841fe338d2bcbbdb27e37b5349423a491f119386c152663f506025d4a00566.jpg)

Even still, until I buckled down and got curious about [BrainFi](https://bradydale.com/series-brainfi-gets-in-your-head.html), I had not encountered the name Alfred Bester. Which is too bad! I had for sure heard the title of this book, *[The Stars My Destination](https://www.audible.com/pd/The-Stars-My-Destination-Audiobook/B077P97JCL)*, because it is such a romantic title. But I didn't have any curiosity about it.

What's really unfortunate about my failure to discover it is [that Bester's book is so close](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Stars_My_Destination) to my teenage interests in superheros. This is a universe where people have *powers*. Almost everyone can teleport themselves around the world. Some people are a little bit psychic. A very few people are fully telepathic.

But what I love about it now is that it points to a future where the next wave of human potential will arrive not from something we build, but **through a latent potential we fulfill.**

* The novel imagines a frontier we've not seriously contemplated: our access to consciousness.

The books main character is Gulliver Foyle. At the start of the book, we are told he is as average as average can be. Just the epitome of the very normal working man. But he has an awakening in the opening pages, when he's treated to an injustice that he won't let go of. That awakening is the first of many awakenings.

In order to seek a right to the way he was wronged, Foyle sets about changing himself in all the ways he needs to so that one man can defeat a massive and powerful system of wealth and power.

Who knows if our brains have anything like the power that Bester imagines here, but I like to think that [there's more to unlock](https://www.frontstageexit.com/p/michael-levin-is-the-most-interesting), if only someone could figure out the right way to try.

In a book deeply concerned with the experience of being alive — which resides in the brain — the protagonist gets confronted with a unique problem: How can he get revenge on a man whose body is alive but whose central nervous system has been switched entirely off?

* 🤯

**Having completed the audiobook,** it never quits raising the stakes. Eventually it indicts the nature of all reality. It rises to heights I never would have expected from the way it begins.

## This book is prophecy.

I may be wrong. If I'm right, I very well may not live to see it. But I think this book is prophecy. I think this book anticipates something about the real potential of conscious experience.

*The Stars My Destination* could well be **the most important BrainFi book** of them all.

—Brady Dale  
October 18, 2026

**Next BrainFi:** [Wire up, lock in](https://bradydale.com/108.html)
